sections.name: summary
sections.label: In short
sections.content: Affirmation by fork turned the human layer into a second copy of the data, and the owner's attention into the single sink.

sections.name: body
sections.label: The evidence
sections.content: Measured 2026-10-30: 304 of the 313 affirmed records are copies of a suggestion, a fifth of all typed records; 133 of 137 problems exist twice; all 24 clusters were forked; 78 poles and 29 tensions still wait (finding da9d4da6). One round affirmed 90 records in one pull request (srs-programme#332), and session logs show seven ratifications in 47 seconds. The owner: "A constant loop of affirmations is actually harder than sitting down and doing the writing" (SP-102); "I cannot affirm a pole on its own" (SP-98); "by the time I get to affirmation, context has often been lost" (f6846947); "the same decision coming back again and again" (36c0549e, SP-64). SP-113: all 254 merges went through the owner, and each fix moved the act instead of removing it. SP-100, SP-101 and SP-103 complete the picture: the owner cannot tell what is asked, the method came before its tools, and understanding has no place to grow as a story.

sections.name: open
sections.label: Open
sections.content: If affirmation becomes optional, do the 304 pairs collapse into one record each, or does an affirmed copy survive only as the tip?
